method: Warp length per item is the finished length plus the take-up and shrinkage allowance: finished length x (1 + allowance / 100). The total warp is the item warp multiplied by the number of items, plus the loom waste and fringe once at the start of the warp. Ends in the warp are the sett in ends per inch multiplied by the width in the reed, rounded to a whole end (half up). Warp yarn is ends x total warp length, converted from inches to yards (divide by 36) and to metres (x 0.0254). The reed table lists reeds of 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20 and 25 dents per inch with the closest whole number of ends per dent from 1 to 4, since sleying more than one end per dent is how weavers reach a sett a single dent pattern cannot give. Lengths are limited to 1-200 in per item, 0-120 in of waste, 1-200 items, a 0-50% allowance, a sett of 1-60 ends per inch and a reed width of 1-120 in. The allowance is one planning figure because take-up and shrinkage depend on weave structure, yarn and finishing; fringe and sampling are not modelled. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Handweaving warp planning: warp length = finished length x (1 + take-up allowance) + loom waste, with the waste and fringe counted once for the whole warp
Sett (ends per inch) x width in the reed = number of warp ends; common reeds are sleyed with 1-4 ends per dent to reach a target sett
